wstep: This card describes the NCHFP recipe for golden pepper jelly: yellow bell peppers and serrano chiles cooked in 5% vinegar, made into a jelly with sugar and liquid pectin and processed in a boiling-water bath. [T:ACI-284,ACI-286,ACI-288]

sekcje.naglowek: Why you must not change the recipe
akapity: The FDA list gives peppers a pH of about 4.65–5.45. [T:ACI-094]
Adding vinegar to the low-acid sweet and hot peppers is what makes this recipe safe for a boiling-water bath; do not reduce the amount of vinegar. [T:ACI-291]
The amounts of vinegar and sugar are also needed for the pectin to form a gel. [T:ACI-291]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): do not change the amounts of vinegar, peppers or sugar; the recipe is tested only in the proportions given. [T:ACI-265]
White distilled vinegar and cider vinegar of 5% acidity are recommended for pickles. [T:ACI-018]
Penn State Extension advises vinegar of 5–7% acidity for home food preservation and advises against diluting vinegar with water unless a research-tested recipe says so. [T:ACI-209,ACI-210]

JarAtlas rule (cautious, for readers outside the USA): use white distilled (spirit) vinegar or cider vinegar labelled 5% or 6% acidity; do not use 10% vinegar and do not dilute it with water to make 5% vinegar; add only the water the recipe lists. [T:ACI-211,ACI-018]
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml. [T:ACI-195]

For about 5 half-pint jars NCHFP uses 5 cups of chopped yellow bell peppers (about 4 large, fleshy peppers), 1/2 cup of chopped serrano chiles (about 5 peppers), 1 1/2 cups of white distilled vinegar (5%), 5 cups of sugar and 1 pouch (3 ounces) of liquid pectin. [T:ACI-284]
NCHFP allows sweet peppers of another color, which give the jelly a different color, and other hot peppers; JarAtlas rule: keep the amounts the same. [T:ACI-292,ACI-265]

When handling or cutting hot peppers, wear plastic or rubber gloves and do not touch your face; without gloves, wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water before touching your face or eyes. [T:ACI-267]
Wash all the peppers thoroughly and remove the stems and seeds; leave the membranes in the hot peppers, because that is where the heat is. [T:ACI-285]
Put the sweet and hot peppers in a blender or food processor, add enough vinegar to purée them, and purée. [T:ACI-285]
Put the purée and the remaining vinegar in an 8- to 10-quart saucepan, bring to a boil and boil for 10 minutes. [T:ACI-285]
Remove from the heat and strain through a jelly bag into a bowl; several layers of cheesecloth can be used instead. [T:ACI-285]
Measure 2 1/4 cups of the strained pepper and vinegar juice into the saucepan. [T:ACI-286]
Stir in the sugar until it dissolves and bring back to a boil. [T:ACI-286]
Add the pectin, bring to a full rolling boil and boil hard for 1 minute, stirring constantly. [T:ACI-286]
Remove from the heat and skim off the foam quickly. [T:ACI-286]
JarAtlas uses the optional NCHFP 10-minute process: the jars do not need to be pre-sterilized; wash and rinse them and keep them hot until filling. [T:ACI-288]
NCHFP says this process may give a stronger vacuum in the jar. [T:ACI-288]
Fill the hot jelly immediately into the hot half-pint jars, leaving 1/4 inch (about 0.6 cm) of headspace. [T:ACI-287]
Wipe the jar rims with a damp clean paper towel, put on the lids and process in a boiling-water canner. [T:ACI-287]
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process half-pint jars in a boiling-water bath for 10 minutes. [T:ACI-288,ACI-176]
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased. [T:ACI-015]
At 1001–6000 ft (above 300 m up to 1800 m) process them for 15 minutes. [T:ACI-289,ACI-176]
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process them for 20 minutes. [T:ACI-290,ACI-176]
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m. [T:ACI-176]
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage. [T:ACI-015]
The NCHFP table gives times only for half-pint jars. [T:ACI-288]

JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): half a pint is about 236.6 ml, so a 0.25 l or 0.5 l jar has no tested time in this recipe; use jars of up to 236 ml, for example 0.2 l. [T:ACI-294,ACI-174]
Let the processed jars cool undisturbed for 12 to 24 hours, then check that the lids have sealed. [T:ACI-287]
Keep any jelly left over after filling the jars in the refrigerator. [T:ACI-293]
Once you open a sealed jar, keep the jelly in the refrigerator. [T:ACI-293]
Discard jelly with mold on it; USDA and microbiologists advise against scooping out the mold and eating the rest. [T:SLO-012]
